planName: 15% Body Fat - Rugby Physique & Performance Plan
source: Built from the user's AdminLife Fitness JSON export and its existing running progression.

goal.primaryGoal: Reduce body fat from about 28% toward 15% by 2027-05-31 while preserving as much muscle and strength as possible.
goal.scaleWeight: Secondary metric only; no target body weight.
goal.proteinTarget: About 190-210 g/day as a practical muscle-retention target.
goal.rateOfChange: Use a moderate calorie deficit. If gym performance, recovery and training quality are deteriorating for 2+ weeks, the deficit is probably too aggressive.
measurementProtocol: Take waist measurement every 2 weeks under similar conditions.
Take front, side and back progress photos every 4 weeks in similar lighting.
Use the same body-fat measurement method each time and judge the trend, not single readings.
Track strength on the main lifts; broadly stable strength while waist/body-fat trend falls is a good sign.

checkpoints.target: Clear waist reduction and visible upper-body definition; body-fat trend ideally in the mid-20s.
Noticeably leaner with strength largely maintained; body-fat trend around low-20s is reasonable.
Approaching high-teens if progress has been consistent.
Aim for approximately 15%; accept measurement noise and judge physique/waist/strength together.

trainingPhases.name: Foundation & Return to Running
trainingPhases.focus: Rebuild running tolerance, establish four-day strength consistency, retain muscle and avoid unnecessary fatigue.
trainingPhases.conditioning: Use the existing run plan only. Do not add extra hard conditioning.
trainingPhases.strength: RPE 6-7 for the first two weeks, then RPE 7-8.

trainingPhases.name: 5K Build
trainingPhases.focus: Progress continuous running while building visible rugby-muscle qualities: chest, back, shoulders, traps, legs and glutes.
trainingPhases.strength: Normal listed volume; progress reps before load.
trainingPhases.recoveryPriority: Keep Thursday lower-body work submaximal before Friday running.

trainingPhases.name: 10K Performance Build
trainingPhases.focus: Continue strength while the running plan introduces more performance work and builds to 10K.
trainingPhases.conditioning: Existing run plan only; no extra Saturday HIIT.
trainingPhases.strength: Reduce lower-body volume by one set per main lift when run fatigue accumulates.
trainingPhases.recoveryPriority: Maintain upper-body volume, protect lower-body freshness.

trainingPhases.name: Rugby Engine Build
trainingPhases.focus: Maintain strength and muscle while converting the running base into repeated-effort rugby fitness.
trainingPhases.conditioning: Wednesday easy aerobic run plus Saturday low-impact/sled conditioning.
trainingPhases.strength: Add medicine-ball power primers; keep compound lifts heavy but crisp.
trainingPhases.recoveryPriority: One complete rest day every week.

trainingPhases.name: Lean Rugby Finish
trainingPhases.focus: Arrive leaner, strong and well-conditioned rather than simply lighter.
trainingPhases.conditioning: Wednesday aerobic maintenance plus Saturday straight-line/repeated-effort rugby conditioning.
trainingPhases.strength: Maintain main-lift intensity; trim accessory volume before trimming heavy work.
trainingPhases.recoveryPriority: Avoid turning every session into a maximal effort.

strengthProgression.effortTarget: Most working sets at RPE 7-8, generally 1-3 reps in reserve.
strengthProgression.doubleProgression: When every set reaches the top of the rep range with good form for two exposures, add 2-2.5 kg to upper-body barbell lifts or the smallest available increment; add 2.5-5 kg to lower-body barbell/trap-bar lifts.
strengthProgression.fatLossRule: Maintaining load and reps while body fat falls counts as progress. Do not force PRs during a calorie deficit.
strengthProgression.deloadRule: Every 5th or 6th week, or sooner if performance and recovery clearly fall, reduce working sets by about 40-50% and keep 3-4 reps in reserve for one week.
strengthProgression.runInterferenceRule: On Monday and Friday, do the run and upper-body lift as separate sessions when practical. If performed close together, do the priority session first and keep the second submaximal.
strengthProgression.lowerBodyRule: Thursday lower-body work must not become a max-effort session because Friday includes running.

phaseAdjustments.adjustment: First two weeks at RPE 6-7, then settle at RPE 7-8. Build consistency and technique.

parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at a brisk, comfortable pace.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 3.0 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at an easy pace.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Only progress if the knee remains settled throughout the week.

existingRunPlan.name: Outdoor Week 7 - Mon 26 Oct
existingRunPlan.purpose: Continue building continuous running distance at a controlled pace.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at a brisk, comfortable pace.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 3.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at an easy pace.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Keep pace easy and consistent. Distance is the only progression.

existingRunPlan.name: Outdoor Week 7 - Wed 28 Oct
existingRunPlan.purpose: Consolidate 3.5 km continuous running.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at a brisk, comfortable pace.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 3.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at an easy pace.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Run by effort rather than chasing your watch.

existingRunPlan.name: Outdoor Week 7 - Fri 30 Oct
existingRunPlan.purpose: Complete the 3.5 km week comfortably before progressing.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at a brisk, comfortable pace.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 3.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at an easy pace.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Progress only if there is no accumulating knee soreness or swelling.

existingRunPlan.name: Outdoor Week 8 - Mon 2 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Build continuous running endurance towards the first 5K.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at a brisk, comfortable pace.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 4.0 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at an easy pace.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Do not increase speed simply because 4 km is starting to feel achievable.

existingRunPlan.name: Outdoor Week 8 - Wed 4 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Consolidate 4 km continuous running.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at a brisk, comfortable pace.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 4.0 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at an easy pace.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Keep the effort comfortable and repeatable.

existingRunPlan.name: Outdoor Week 8 - Fri 6 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Complete a full week at 4 km before attempting longer distances.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at a brisk, comfortable pace.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 4.0 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at an easy pace.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Finish comfortably rather than testing how fast you can run 4 km.

existingRunPlan.name: 5K Goal Week - Mon 9 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Complete the final distance progression before the first 5K.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at a brisk, comfortable pace.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 4.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at an easy pace.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Treat this as an easy endurance run, not a 4.5 km time trial.

existingRunPlan.name: 5K Goal Week - Wed 11 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Reduce running volume before the first continuous 5K while maintaining rhythm.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at a brisk, comfortable pace.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 3.0 km continuously at a very easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at an easy pace.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: This is deliberately shorter. Do not run hard. Finish fresh and leave Thursday as a non-running day.

existingRunPlan.name: First Continuous 5K - Fri 13 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Complete the first continuous 5K comfortably and without treating it as a race.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at a brisk, comfortable pace.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 5.0 km continuously at an easy conversational effort. Start conservatively. A pace around 8:15-8:45 min/km is completely acceptable, and slower is fine.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk 0.5 km at an easy pace.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: The goal is simply to complete 5 km continuously with the knee feeling good. Do not race it. If the knee has reacted during the preceding week, postpone the 5K and repeat the previous successful week instead.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 1 - Easy Run - Mon 16 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Recover from the first 5K while beginning the transition from rehabilitation running to normal aerobic training.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min, then complete a few ankle rolls, leg swings and easy marching drills.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 4.0 km continuously at an easy conversational effort. Aim roughly for 8:00-8:40 min/km, but do not force the pace.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: This should feel easier than the previous 5K. Keep the effort around RPE 3-4/10 and finish feeling capable of running farther.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 1 - Faster Running - Wed 18 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Introduce controlled faster running without the intensity of a true hard interval session.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk for 3 min, then jog easily for 7 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 5 x 90 sec at a controlled faster pace of roughly 7:40-8:00 min/km. Recover with 2 min very easy jogging or walking after each effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Jog very easily for 5 min, then walk for 3 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: The faster portions should feel smooth rather than hard. Aim for RPE 5-6/10 and never sprint.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 1 - Long Run - Fri 20 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Begin extending running endurance beyond the previous 5K maximum.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 5.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort. Aim roughly for 8:05-8:40 min/km.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Treat the extra 0.5 km as the progression. Do not also try to make this faster than your normal easy pace.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 2 - Easy Run - Mon 23 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Build repeatable aerobic running volume without creating excessive fatigue.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 4.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort. Aim roughly for 8:00-8:35 min/km.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Keep this deliberately easy so you are fresh enough for Wednesday's faster work.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 2 - Intervals - Wed 25 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Develop running speed and aerobic power through short controlled repetitions.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk for 3 min, jog easily for 7 min, then complete 2 x 20 sec relaxed faster strides.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 6 x 2 min at roughly 7:30-7:50 min/km. Recover with 2 min easy jogging or walking after each repetition.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Jog easily for 5 min, then walk for 3 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Aim for RPE 6/10. You should finish the final repetition feeling that you could complete one more.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 2 - Long Run - Fri 27 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Continue gradually extending continuous running endurance.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 6.0 km continuously at an easy conversational effort. Aim roughly for 8:05-8:40 min/km.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Keep the first kilometre particularly easy. The goal is comfortable distance, not pace.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 3 - Easy Run - Mon 30 Nov
existingRunPlan.purpose: Develop aerobic fitness while increasing normal weekly running volume.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 5.0 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: A 5K is now a normal easy training run rather than a goal effort.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 3 - Tempo Intervals - Wed 2 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Introduce sustained moderately hard running and improve the pace that can be maintained aerobically.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk for 3 min followed by 8 min of easy jogging.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 3 x 5 min at controlled tempo effort, approximately 7:30-7:50 min/km. Take 3 min easy jogging between repetitions.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Jog easily for 6 min, then walk for 3 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Tempo should feel like RPE 6-7/10: working, but controlled and nowhere near an all-out effort.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 3 - Long Run - Fri 4 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Build endurance beyond 6 km while maintaining an easy aerobic effort.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 6.5 km continuously at an easy conversational pace.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Do not speed up at the end. Keep the entire run comfortably aerobic.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 4 - Easy Run - Mon 7 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Reduce running load temporarily to consolidate the previous three weeks of training.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 4.0 km continuously at a relaxed conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: This is a deliberate easier week. Do not add additional distance because you feel good.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 4 - Speed Introduction - Wed 9 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Develop leg turnover through short faster efforts while keeping overall training load low.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk for 3 min and jog easily for 8 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 6 x 1 min at approximately 7:15-7:35 min/km with 2 min easy jogging between repetitions.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Jog easily for 5 min, then walk for 3 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Run quickly but smoothly. This is not sprinting and should never feel uncontrolled.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 4 - Long Run - Fri 11 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Complete a reduced-distance long run before the next training build.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 5.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: This completes the deload week. Finish feeling fresh.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 5 - Easy Run - Mon 14 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Return to normal aerobic running volume following the lighter week.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 5.0 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Keep the pace relaxed. Faster running belongs in Wednesday's session.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 5 - Tempo Intervals - Wed 16 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Increase the amount of sustained faster running that can be completed comfortably.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk for 3 min followed by 8 min easy jogging.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 4 x 5 min at approximately 7:25-7:45 min/km with 2 min 30 sec easy jogging between repetitions.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Jog easily for 6 min, then walk for 3 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Keep all four repetitions similar. If the first is dramatically faster than the fourth, you started too quickly.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 5 - Long Run - Fri 18 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Extend continuous endurance to 7 km.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 7.0 km continuously at a conversational effort. Aim roughly for 8:00-8:35 min/km.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Keep enough in reserve that the final kilometre feels no harder than the middle of the run.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 6 - Easy Run - Mon 21 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Maintain aerobic fitness through the holiday period without increasing training stress.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 4.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Keep this simple and comfortable.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 6 - Steady Run - Wed 23 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Learn to hold a moderately quicker pace continuously rather than relying only on intervals.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Run approximately 1.5 km very easily after a short walking warm-up.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run continuously for 20 min at a steady effort of roughly 7:40-8:00 min/km.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Run approximately 1.0 km easily, then walk for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: This should feel stronger than easy running but clearly easier than a race effort.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 6 - Long Run - Fri 25 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Maintain long-run endurance without increasing distance during the holiday week.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 6.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Move this to Thu 24 Dec or Sat 26 Dec if Christmas Day does not suit. Do not attempt to make up missed running.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 7 - Easy Run - Mon 28 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Return to normal training volume while maintaining good recovery.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 5.0 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: The easy run should remain genuinely easy even as fitness improves.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 7 - Threshold Intervals - Wed 30 Dec
existingRunPlan.purpose: Improve the ability to sustain faster running by accumulating controlled threshold work.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk for 3 min followed by 10 min easy jogging.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 5 x 3 min at approximately 7:15-7:35 min/km with 2 min easy jogging between repetitions.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Jog easily for 7 min, then walk for 3 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Aim around RPE 7/10. The repetitions should be hard enough to require concentration but not feel like maximum efforts.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 7 - Long Run - Fri 1 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Increase endurance towards 8 km while keeping the run comfortably aerobic.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 7.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Move this by a day if New Year's Day does not suit. Do not combine it with Wednesday's faster session.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 8 - Easy Run - Mon 4 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Reduce training volume to consolidate the previous three-week build.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 4.5 km continuously at a relaxed conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Treat this as recovery training rather than an opportunity to run faster.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 8 - Fartlek - Wed 6 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Improve speed and running economy through short relaxed bursts of quicker running.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk for 3 min followed by 10 min easy jogging.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 8 x 1 min at approximately 7:05-7:25 min/km with 90 sec very easy jogging between repetitions.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Jog easily for 6 min, then walk for 3 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Stay relaxed through the shoulders and avoid turning the one-minute efforts into sprints.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 8 - Long Run - Fri 8 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Complete a shorter long run during the deload week.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 6.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Finish the week feeling fresher than you started it.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 9 - Easy Run - Mon 11 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Increase normal aerobic running volume as fitness improves.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 5.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Allow the pace to improve naturally but keep the effort around RPE 3-4/10.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 9 - Tempo Intervals - Wed 13 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Build sustained speed and improve the pace that can be held for longer distances.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk for 3 min followed by 10 min easy jogging.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 3 x 8 min at approximately 7:20-7:40 min/km with 3 min easy jogging between repetitions.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Jog easily for 7 min, then walk for 3 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Aim for a pace you could theoretically maintain for considerably longer than eight minutes.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 9 - Long Run - Fri 15 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Reach 8 km continuous running while maintaining an easy aerobic effort.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 8.0 km continuously at an easy conversational effort. Approximately 7:55-8:30 min/km is a reasonable guide if comfortable.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Fuel and hydrate normally beforehand. The distance, not speed, is the progression.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 10 - Easy Run - Mon 18 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Maintain aerobic volume while recovering from the longer run.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 5.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Keep this relaxed even if your normal pace is beginning to become noticeably faster.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 10 - Threshold Intervals - Wed 20 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Develop faster sustained running and improve cardiovascular capacity.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk for 3 min followed by 10 min easy jogging and 2 x 20 sec relaxed strides.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 6 x 3 min at approximately 7:10-7:30 min/km with 2 min easy jogging between repetitions.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Jog easily for 7 min, then walk for 3 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: The goal is six consistent repetitions. Do not chase the fastest possible split.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 10 - Long Run - Fri 22 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Extend continuous endurance beyond 8 km.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 8.5 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Do not add a fast finish. Keep the whole session aerobic.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 11 - Easy Run & Strides - Mon 25 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Build aerobic volume while adding small amounts of relaxed speed and improving running economy.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 6.0 km easily. During the final 2 km, include 4 x 20 sec relaxed strides with at least 90 sec of easy running between each.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Strides should feel quick, light and smooth rather than exhausting.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 11 - Continuous Tempo - Wed 27 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Develop the ability to hold a meaningfully faster pace continuously.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Run 1.5-2.0 km very easily after a short walking warm-up.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run continuously for 20 min at approximately 7:20-7:40 min/km or RPE 6-7/10.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Jog easily until approximately 6 km total running distance, then walk for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: This should be your strongest sustained training run so far, but you should never be hanging on desperately at the end.

existingRunPlan.name: Performance Week 11 - Long Run - Fri 29 Jan
existingRunPlan.purpose: Complete the final major endurance progression before attempting 10 km.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 9.0 km continuously at an easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Keep the pace comfortable. If 9 km feels manageable rather than heroic, the training is doing exactly what it should.

existingRunPlan.name: 10K Goal Week - Easy Run - Mon 1 Feb
existingRunPlan.purpose: Reduce fatigue while maintaining normal running rhythm before the first 10K.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 4.0 km continuously at a very easy conversational effort.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Deliberately hold back. This week is about arriving fresh for Friday.

existingRunPlan.name: 10K Goal Week - Easy Run & Strides - Wed 3 Feb
existingRunPlan.purpose: Keep the legs moving while adding a small amount of faster running before the 10K.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5 min.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 3.0 km easily. During the second half complete 4 x 30 sec relaxed faster strides with 90 sec easy running between each.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for 5 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: Do not turn this into a workout. The strides should make the legs feel better rather than tired.

existingRunPlan.name: First Continuous 10K - Fri 5 Feb
existingRunPlan.purpose: Complete the first continuous 10 km and establish a new endurance baseline for future performance training.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: Walk briskly for 5-8 min, then complete a few leg swings and ankle mobility drills.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 10.0 km continuously. Start conservatively at roughly 8:00-8:30 min/km or whatever pace feels genuinely easy. If you still feel strong after 8 km, allow the final 2 km to become gradually quicker.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: Walk easily for at least 5-10 min.

existingRunPlan.howToUse: This is not a 10K race. The goal is to finish continuously and under control. If your knee has become sore, swollen or increasingly stiff during the preceding weeks, postpone the attempt and repeat the most recent successful week.

post10KSessionLibrary.name: Wednesday Aerobic Run
post10KSessionLibrary.purpose: Maintain the aerobic base built by the 10K plan while leaving enough recovery for strength and rugby conditioning.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: 8-10 min brisk walk and easy jog plus Pre-Run Dynamic Mobility.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: Run 4-6 km at an easy conversational effort. Every second week, finish with 4-6 x 15 sec relaxed strides at about 80-85% speed with a full walk-back recovery.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: 5 min easy walk.

post10KSessionLibrary.howToUse: Keep this genuinely aerobic. It should not compete with Thursday lower-body training.

post10KSessionLibrary.name: Rugby Conditioning - Low Impact Repeat Efforts
post10KSessionLibrary.purpose: Introduce repeated hard efforts with minimal running impact after the 10K base is complete.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: 8 min easy assault bike or spin bike, gradually building cadence.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 8 x 30 sec hard at RPE 8-9 followed by 90 sec very easy. Keep output repeatable rather than sprinting the first rep all-out.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: 5 min very easy spin.

post10KSessionLibrary.howToUse: Use through February. Stop the set if power falls sharply or form deteriorates.

post10KSessionLibrary.name: Rugby Conditioning - Sled & Bike
post10KSessionLibrary.purpose: Build leg drive and repeated-effort capacity with rugby-relevant resistance.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: 8 min easy bike plus dynamic lower-body mobility.

parts.name: Sled block
parts.detail: 6 x 15-20 m heavy sled push. Walk back and rest until breathing is controlled.

parts.name: Bike block
parts.detail: 6 x 20 sec hard assault-bike effort followed by 70 sec easy.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: 5 min easy walk or bike.

post10KSessionLibrary.howToUse: Use through March. The sled should be heavy enough to require force but not so heavy that posture collapses.

post10KSessionLibrary.name: Rugby Conditioning - Straight-Line Tempo
post10KSessionLibrary.purpose: Reintroduce faster running in controlled straight-line efforts without jumping immediately to maximal sprinting or sharp cutting.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: 10 min easy jog, dynamic mobility and 3 gradual 40-60 m build-ups.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 2 sets of 6 x 20 sec at about 75-80% running speed, followed by 40 sec walk. Rest 3 min between sets.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: 5-10 min easy walk.

post10KSessionLibrary.howToUse: Use through April only if the knee remains settled during running and the following morning. Otherwise use Low Impact Repeat Efforts.

post10KSessionLibrary.name: Rugby Conditioning - Repeated Efforts
post10KSessionLibrary.purpose: Prepare for the repeated high-output work-rest pattern of rugby while keeping efforts controlled rather than maximal.

parts.name: Warm-up
parts.detail: 10 min easy jog plus dynamic mobility and gradual accelerations.

parts.name: Main set
parts.detail: 3 sets of 5 x 20 sec hard at about 80-85% speed followed by 40 sec walk/jog. Rest 3 min between sets.

parts.name: Optional progression
parts.detail: Only if fully comfortable with straight-line work: make 2-3 reps per set gentle 10-20 m shuttle patterns rather than all reps. Avoid maximal cutting.

parts.name: Cool-down
parts.detail: 8 min easy walk.

post10KSessionLibrary.howToUse: Use through May. Quality is more important than exhaustion.

library.name: Easy Recovery Walk
library.purpose: Promote circulation and reduce general stiffness without adding training fatigue.
library.notes: Walk on a flat route at a comfortable conversational pace. Keep the effort deliberately easy.

library.name: Easy Recovery Bike
library.purpose: Increase blood flow through tired legs after running, rugby or lower-body training.
library.notes: Use very light resistance and a relaxed cadence. You should finish feeling fresher than when you started.

library.name: Pool Recovery
library.purpose: Move the body and promote circulation with minimal impact on the joints.
library.notes: Alternate easy swimming, gentle pool walking and relaxed floating. Avoid hard lengths or structured intervals.

library.name: Sauna Recovery
library.purpose: Relax and wind down following training.
library.notes: Use one or two comfortable rounds. Drink water before and afterwards, and leave if you feel dizzy or unwell.

library.name: Hot Bath Recovery
library.purpose: Relax tired muscles and help the body settle before bed.
library.notes: Use comfortably warm water rather than extreme heat. Follow it with water and a relaxed evening.

library.name: Foam Rolling Recovery
library.purpose: Reduce the feeling of soreness and tightness in heavily trained muscles.
library.notes: Roll the calves, quads, hamstrings, glutes and upper back. Use moderate pressure and avoid rolling directly over painful joints.

library.name: Breathing and Relaxation
library.purpose: Bring the body down from a hard session and support relaxation before sleep.
library.notes: Lie somewhere comfortable and breathe slowly through your nose. Keep the exhale slightly longer than the inhale.

library.name: Legs-Up Recovery
library.purpose: Provide a simple period of rest after spending a long time running, walking or standing.
library.notes: Lie on your back with your lower legs supported on a sofa or against a wall. Relax and breathe normally.

library.name: Recovery Nap
library.purpose: Reduce tiredness and improve alertness after demanding training or poor sleep.
library.notes: Keep the nap around 20 to 30 minutes and avoid taking it too close to bedtime.

library.name: Post-Training Recovery Routine
library.purpose: Begin the recovery process immediately after a demanding gym, running or rugby session.
library.notes: Complete 10 minutes of easy walking or cycling, drink water, eat a meal containing protein and carbohydrates, then spend the remainder relaxing.

library.name: Low-Stimulation Evening
library.purpose: Improve sleep readiness and support recovery from accumulated training fatigue.
library.notes: Dim the lights, reduce phone use, avoid intense exercise and complete a quiet activity such as reading, listening to music or taking a warm shower.

library.name: Complete Rest Day
library.purpose: Allow physical and mental fatigue to settle without adding more structured exercise.
library.notes: Skip formal training. Focus on normal daily movement, regular meals, hydration and getting a full night of sleep.

readinessRules: Do not add extra hard conditioning before the existing 10K plan is complete.
If running causes a meaningful increase in knee pain, swelling, altered gait or next-morning stiffness, repeat or regress the running week and skip the optional hard conditioning.
If two consecutive strength sessions show a clear drop in performance and sleep/leg soreness are poor, take a deload or remove one accessory set from each workout for a week.
Hard conditioning should finish with repeatable output. Stop before it becomes sloppy survival work.
Do not perform maximal sprinting or sharp change-of-direction work until straight-line running and tempo work are consistently symptom-free.
